translationRepairs: He was born at Diaoke, in the Huairou garrison of Guizhou.
He was born at Diaoke, in the Huairong garrison of Guizhou.
The source reads Huairong, not Huairou. Correct the name while retaining the intelligible idiomatic rendering garrison for the military settlement.
He was born at Diaoke village in Huairou Army of Guizhou.
He was born at Diaoke village in Huairong Army of Guizhou.
The source reads Huairong, not Huairou. Correct the name while retaining the intelligible idiomatic rendering garrison for the military settlement.
His great-grandfather Shunli had served for generations as garrison troops at Huairou.
His great-grandfather was Shunli; the family had served in the Huairong garrison for generations.
The place is Huairong. Generational garrison service belongs to the family, not multiple generations lived by one great-grandfather; distinguish Shunli from that hereditary service.
When the Liang general Liu Yan held Xin, he faced the Taiyuan army in a standoff and skirmished from morning to night.
When the Liang general Liu Xun held Xin, he faced the Taiyuan army in a standoff and skirmished from morning to night.
The general is Liu Xun, written Liu plus the character for Xun, not Liu Yan. The false English spelling is a translation error, not a source-attested alternate name.
When Mingzong stormed Yanzhou, Xingzhou led the vanguard.
When Mingzong stormed Yunzhou, Xingzhou led the vanguard.
The written prefecture is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou. Correct only this place name and the directly dependent event claim.
When Mingzong attacked Yanzhou, Xingzhou served as vanguard.
When Mingzong attacked Yunzhou, Xingzhou served as vanguard.
The written prefecture is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou. Correct only this place name and the directly dependent event claim.
Early in the Changxing era, because the northern frontier bordered the Rong and Wang tribes, he was appointed military commissioner of Zhenwu.
Early in the Changxing era, because the northern frontier bordered the Rong king's territory, he was appointed military commissioner of Zhenwu.
The source says the Rong king, not separate Rong and Wang peoples. Retain this source designation without inventing a personal identity for the ruler; frontier proximity concerns his territory.
At the beginning of the Changxing era, because the northern border neighbored the Rong and Wang peoples, he was appointed military commissioner of Zhenwu.
At the beginning of the Changxing era, because the northern border adjoined the Rong king's territory, he was appointed military commissioner of Zhenwu.
The source says the Rong king, not separate Rong and Wang peoples. Retain this source designation without inventing a personal identity for the ruler; frontier proximity concerns his territory.
After that Yang no longer dared to act—but Jingda was still killed by the traitor Guangyuan.
After that Xingzhou no longer dared to keep guarding him, and Jingda was then killed by Guangyuan.

In s0039 Xingzhou places guards around Jingda; s0040 has Jingda questioning why Xingzhou follows him. Thus the omitted subject of no longer daring to do so is Xingzhou, who stops the protective action, not Yang Guangyuan. The final clause says Guangyuan killed Jingda without an additional narrator epithet.
When the emperor returned to the capital, he replaced Jing Yanguang as commander of the palace guard and was made military commissioner of Yanzhou.
When the emperor returned to the capital, he replaced Jing Yanguang as commander of the palace guard and was made military commissioner of Yunzhou.
The source names Yunzhou, as in the earlier capture, not Yanzhou.
When Emperor Gaozu of Han entered Bian, Xingzhou was made acting Grand Tutor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, replacing Li Shouzhen as military commissioner of the Pingping circuit.
When Emperor Gaozu of Han entered Bian, Xingzhou was made acting Grand Tutor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, replacing Li Shouzhen as military commissioner of the Tianping circuit.
The source circuit is Tianping, not Pingping; retain the surrounding wording and do not attach this later event to the ancient Han founder.
In the Qianyou era he came to court, was made acting Grand Preceptor, was advanced to Prince of Ye, was again granted the Pingping commissioner seal and command, and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.
In the Qianyou era he came to court, was made acting Grand Preceptor, was advanced to Prince of Ye, was again granted the Tianping commissioner seal and command, and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.
The commissioner command is Tianping, not Pingping.
His great-grandfather Shunli had garrisoned Huairou for generations.
His great-grandfather was Shunli; the family had garrisoned Huairong for generations.

Accept. The nominal clause identifies Shunli as the great-grandfather. The following hereditary predicate describes the family serving over successive generations, not one man garrisoning for multiple lifetimes. The family subject is a justified English explication; Huairong represents the written place. This approves neither an individual service date nor a new genealogical person.
When the Liang general Liu Yan held Xin, he faced the Taiyuan army across the lines and fought day and night.
When the Liang general Liu Xun held Xin, he faced the Taiyuan army across the lines and fought day and night.

Accept the bounded Liu Yan to Liu Xun correction: the source explicitly names Liu Xun. The adjacent rescue episode and the parallel account in Zizhitongjian 269 concern the same Liang commander. Xin is a separate surviving place-name error, recorded only as an unapproved supplemental proposal; it is not newly endorsed by this bounded name repair.
From this Yang no longer dared to act, but Jingda was nevertheless killed by Guangyuan.
From this Xingzhou no longer dared to keep guarding him, and Jingda was then killed by Guangyuan.

Accept. In s0039 Yang Guangyuan plots against Jingda while Xingzhou brings men to protect him. In s0040 Jingda questions why Xingzhou follows him, not knowing this is protection. The omitted subject in s0041 is therefore Xingzhou, and doing so resumes his protective attendance. The result clause states that Guangyuan killed Jingda. Assigning the first clause to Yang and translating the result as nevertheless reverses the causal chain. Keep guarding him is warranted contextual explication.
When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, he replaced Jing Yanguang as commander of the palace guard and was made military commissioner of Yanzhou.
When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, he replaced Jing Yanguang as commander of the palace guard and was made military commissioner of Yunzhou.

Accept. The written prefecture is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou. The same distinction occurs in s0026 and s0197; the source elsewhere writes the different Yan character when it means Yan. Only the paired literal place name changes; the existing office claim already has Yunzhou.
When Emperor Gaozu of Han entered Bian, Xingzhou was made acting Grand Tutor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, replacing Li Shouzhen as military commissioner of the Pingping circuit.
When Emperor Gaozu of Han entered Bian, Xingzhou was made acting Grand Tutor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, replacing Li Shouzhen as military commissioner of the Tianping circuit.

Accept. The circuit name is Tianping, literally the written Tian and Ping, not Pingping. The appointment replaces Li Shouzhen. The existing idiomatic field and relevant office labels already have Tianping. This is not a new identity decision about the Han founder.
In the Qianyou era he came to court, was made acting Grand Preceptor, was advanced to Prince of Ye, was again granted the Pingping commissioner seal and command, and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.

Accept. The source repeats Tianping in the grant of the commissioner command. Correcting Pingping restores that proper name without changing the chronology, princely titles, or surrounding office wording.
